Inside the modelsFormulas, propagation & conventions

The two local models

APD: P(x) = f(x₀) + Δf(x₀; x − x₀). At every smooth node, freeze its derivative at the original reference value. Keep absolute-value operations exact on the propagated model.

AD: A(x) = f(x₀) + gᵀ(x − x₀). It propagates a single chosen slope through each switching operation.

For two inputs, x and x₀ in these formulas denote vectors. APD is a local approximation; moving far from the reference can give large errors. The computational expression matters, even for algebraically equivalent functions.

Kinks and domains

We define abs′(0) = s with selectable s ∈ {−1, 0, 1}. ReLU is treated as (u + |u|)/2, and max/min as (a + b ± |a − b|)/2. Thus at a tie, ReLU uses (1+s)/2; max uses weights ((1+s)/2, (1−s)/2), with the weights reversed for min. This is an explicit implementation convention, and may differ from your AD library. A chosen AD slope is not a unique derivative at a kink.

Every smooth elemental operation must have a finite value and derivative at the reference. Invalid original-function samples are omitted; the affine models may extend beyond the original domain. APD lines and surfaces are split at their computed switching points (up to floating-point precision). The original function and error maps use finite sample grids: very narrow features or poles may require a smaller visible domain.

Method: Griewank et al., Piecewise linear secant approximation via algorithmic piecewise differentiation, §2. This explorer implements its single-reference tangent construction.
